Read these first, in full, and follow them:

- `/tmp/bb-provider-bridge-provider-claude-code-OGhMjQ/skills/bb-claude-skill-plugins-zFP9i9/8045f4d6b154b804/skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md`
- `AGENTS.md` at the repo root of your worktree
- `.agents/skills/verify-chauvenity-os/features/greeter-login.md`

# The user's goal

The user is adding animated fireflies to their lock and login screens in
ekans/dotfiles, in PR https://github.com/ekans/dotfiles/pull/23 (open, not
merged). The login screen in chauvenity-os is a copy of the dotfiles greeter,
made by `scripts/sync-greeter.sh` and committed under
`files/system/etc/xdg/quickshell/`. They want this repo ready for that PR, so
the next sync cannot ship a login screen that fails to load.

# The problem, and its root cause

`scripts/sync-greeter.sh` copies a hardcoded list of five files. PR #23 adds
`chauvenity-lock/LockScene.qml`, `chauvenity-lock/Firefly.qml` and
`chauvenity-lock/art/*.png`, which the new `LockFace.qml` uses. A sync with
today's list copies the new `LockFace.qml` and leaves those behind, and
Quickshell then fails with `LockScene is not a type`: no login screen at all,
with nothing warning whoever ran the sync.

The root cause is a category error in the script. QML loads these as
**directories**, not as files: `chauvenity-greeter/GreeterFace.qml` says
`import "lock"`, which makes every `.qml` file beside `LockFace.qml` a type.
A per-file allow list cannot track a directory-wide import, so it goes stale
silently. Making today's list longer would bring the trap back on the next
file added.

# What to build

One file changes the behaviour: `scripts/sync-greeter.sh`. Rewrite it around
the directory as the unit, with a load gate after the copy. Two parts, both
needed, because each covers a class the other misses (measured, see below).

## Part 1: copy the directory, name what stays behind

Copy every file under `$src/chauvenity-greeter` and `$src/chauvenity-lock`
(where `$src` is `DOTFILES_CHECKOUT/quickshell`), except these paths, each of
which gets a one-line reason in the code:

- `chauvenity-greeter/tests/*` and `chauvenity-lock/tests/*` — run from the
  dotfiles checkout, never loaded by the greeter.
- `chauvenity-lock/shell.qml` — the lock's own entry point. The greeter never
  loads it, and `/etc/xdg` is an XDG config dir, so shipping it would make
  `qs -c chauvenity-lock` resolve to an image config nothing in the image
  starts.
- `chauvenity-lock/lock.sh` — starts the user's lock session; the greeter
  never runs it.
- `chauvenity-lock/art/sprites.sh` — regenerates `art/*.png`, which ship
  already drawn.

Drift now runs in the safe direction: a file added to either directory ships
without anyone touching this script, and shipping one extra file is harmless
where missing one is fatal.

Keep the existing check that `$src/chauvenity-greeter/lock` is a symlink to
`../chauvenity-lock`, and keep recreating that symlink in the destination.
`find -type f` does not follow it, so the lock directory is copied by its own
pass; do not copy through the symlink. Files install with mode 644 as today
(`install -D -m 644` handles the PNGs fine).

## Part 2: load the copy before installing it

Build into a staging directory (`mktemp -d`, removed by a trap), gate the
staging tree, and only then replace `files/system/etc/xdg/quickshell/
chauvenity-greeter` and `.../chauvenity-lock`. A failed gate must leave the
repo's `files/` untouched and exit non-zero. Do not touch
`files/system/etc/xdg/quickshell/chauvenity/`, which is the bar, not the
greeter.

The gate, measured on this machine today, exit code 255 in every case and
0.1 s per run:

    timeout 120 env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY -u DISPLAY -u GREETD_SOCK \
      QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen qs -p "$stage/chauvenity-greeter" --no-color 2>&1

Qt's offscreen platform has no layer-shell, so Quickshell refuses the
greeter's `PanelWindow`. Everything before that has already run: every QML
document the greeter reaches is compiled and every type and script resolved.
So a complete tree produces exactly this, and nothing else:

     ERROR: Failed to load configuration
     ERROR:   caused by @shell.qml[211:9]: No PanelWindow backend loaded.

while an incomplete one names what it could not reach, for example:

     ERROR:   caused by @lock/LockFace.qml[76:5]: LockScene is not a type
     ERROR:   caused by @greeter.mjs[-1:-1]: File not found

Pass only when the log contains the `No PanelWindow backend loaded` line and
no other `ERROR:` line besides the `Failed to load configuration` header. The
exit code says nothing (255 either way), so read the log. On failure, print
the whole log to stderr and say that nothing was installed.

What the gate cannot catch, and must not be claimed to: a missing
`art/*.png`. Measured — deleting `art/glow.png` still produces the clean
`No PanelWindow backend loaded` log, because the window never maps and the
image is never loaded. Part 1 is what covers that class. Say so in the
script's header comment, honestly and in one sentence.

## Part 3: the second hardcoded list

`test/image-contract.sh:103` ("the greetd user can read the greeter") names
three files by hand, so it would pass on a tree missing everything else.
Change it to check that the greetd user can read **every** file under
`/etc/xdg/quickshell/chauvenity-greeter/` and
`/etc/xdg/quickshell/chauvenity-lock/`, so a newly shipped file is covered
without editing the check. Match the file's existing `check '<name>' '<shell>'`
style and keep the name short. Leave the other checks alone.

## Docs

`.agents/skills/verify-chauvenity-os/features/greeter-login.md:55` describes
the sync in one line. Update it only if the rewrite makes it wrong. Do not
start a new doc file.

# Hard constraints

- **Do not run the sync into the repo's `files/`.** PR #23 is not merged and
  the image must not ship unmerged dotfiles code. `git status` must show no
  change under `files/` when you are done. Test against a scratch destination
  only.
- Never `pkill`, `killall` or `pgrep -f`-then-kill `qs` or `niri`, not even
  through `niri-sandbox run`. The sandbox shares the process list with the
  user's live niri session; doing that killed their bar once already. Stop a
  Quickshell instance with `qs kill -p <dir>`. The offscreen gate above exits
  on its own and needs no kill.
- Never start `qs` or any GUI app on the user's `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`. The
  offscreen gate has `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset, which is why it is safe here.
- Do not reformat or restructure the rest of the script beyond what the
  rewrite needs.

# Two dotfiles trees to test against, already cloned for you

- `/tmp/greeter-sync-thr_cjwcg2c53u/dotfiles-main` — dotfiles `main`, no
  `LockScene.qml`.
- `/tmp/greeter-sync-thr_cjwcg2c53u/dotfiles-pr23` — PR #23's branch
  `lock-and-login-14-fireflies-thr_x35b5jtbyd`.

The script must work against both, because the order the two PRs land in is
not settled. Do not write to those clones.

# Success criteria

1. `scripts/sync-greeter.sh /tmp/greeter-sync-thr_cjwcg2c53u/dotfiles-main`,
   pointed at a scratch destination, produces exactly today's five files plus
   the `lock` symlink, and nothing else. Verified by hand already: that is the
   expected output.
2. The same against `dotfiles-pr23` additionally produces `LockScene.qml`,
   `Firefly.qml` and the four `art/*.png`, and no `art/sprites.sh`,
   `shell.qml`, `lock.sh` or `tests/`.
3. A tree with `LockScene.qml` removed makes the script exit non-zero, print
   the QML error, and leave the destination unchanged.
4. `bash -n scripts/sync-greeter.sh` and `shellcheck scripts/sync-greeter.sh`
   (if shellcheck is installed) are clean.
5. `git status --porcelain` shows changes only to `scripts/sync-greeter.sh`,
   `test/image-contract.sh`, and the one doc line if you changed it.

Make the destination overridable for testing, in the smallest way that works
(an env var the script reads, documented in its header), so criteria 1 to 3
run without touching `files/`. Do not add a flag parser.

Commit your work on the current branch with a message in the repo's style
(lower-case, `fix(...)` or `feat(...)`, a sentence that says what changed for
whom). Do not open a PR and do not push.

Report back: the diff you wrote, the three runs' output, and anything you
found that the brief got wrong.

---
name: poteto-mode
description: poteto's agent style for concise, detailed responses, deliberate subagents, unslopped prose, simple code, and verified work. Use for poteto, /poteto-mode, or requests to work in this style.
disable-model-invocation: true
icon: crown
color: yellow
---

# Poteto mode

Bundled skills live at `../<name>/SKILL.md` from this file, so put this file's absolute path in every `poteto-agent` prompt.

## Non-negotiables

The Principles section below grounds every trigger. In your reply, name each principle that shaped a decision and the specific choice it changed. Cite only principles whose leaf SKILL.md you read this session.

Remaining triggers:

- Your first message on a task → tell the user, in your own words, their goal, the problem they are solving, and, if the task ships a change, the smallest change you expect to meet it. Don't wait for confirmation. If the evidence rules out the change the user asked for, show it and stop. Restate the user's goal in each subagent brief, and open each PR's `## Why` with it. Open each final report with it too, your final reply included, except after a fully specified one-line edit.
- Nontrivial change, architecture decision, or "are we sure?" → the **how** skill.
- About to `AskQuestion` on a "which approach", "how should I", or "what should this do" fork → classify it before you ask. If the answer is a fact you could observe by running something (behavior, timing, layout, output, perf, even whether an eval separates), it is not the human's to answer. Sketch it via the Prototype playbook (`playbooks/prototype.md`) and let the result decide. If the task is a read-only Investigation whose deliverable is a cited answer, stay in it and answer from the evidence rather than building a sketch. Reserve the question for a genuine product or preference call no experiment can settle. Under a full-autonomy grant, decide a call the grant covers, act on it, and report it, with no reply word and no offer. Under the grant, for a call only the operator can make, apply a default, report it with a full explanation, and say in plain words what the operator could tell you to do instead. The operator answers in their own words. Never give a shorthand token to type back. Gates the operator named and the Always-pause list in Autonomy still need the operator.
- Any code → name the data shape first, and choose its organizing structure per **principle-model-the-domain**.
- Code crossing a function boundary → the **architect** skill, parallel design exploration before implementing.
- Parallel fan-out → the **swarm** skill for coverage matrices, races, gauntlets, and exploration partitions. Use **arena** for design or code bakeoffs with base selection and grafting.
- Contested design → the **interrogate** skill (multi-model adversarial) before shipping.
- Nontrivial multi-step → write the throughput checkpoint (Feature step 3).
- Any prose surface, your reply to the user included → the **unslop** skill. Write the reply per **Writing the reply**. Agent-facing prose also follows the **create-skill** skill (Cursor's built-in for authoring SKILL.md files).
- Docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages → the **technical-writing** skill (`/technical-writing`).
- Before commit → the `deslop` skill from the `cursor-team-kit` plugin (`/deslop`).
- Before review → the **no-comments** skill (`/no-comments`).
- Shipping UI / IDE / CLI → the matching control skill. `cursor-team-kit` publishes `control-cli` (CLIs and TUIs) and `control-ui` (browser / Electron / web UIs). For bug fixes, reproduce first on the same surface yourself. Hand to the user only under the narrow Bug fix step 1 exception.
- Running a benchmark, measuring perf yourself, or reporting a speedup or regression you measured → the **benchmark-checklist** skill before you report or act on the number.
- Any PR-status request ("babysit this", "get it green", "address the bugbot comments", and most often "check on PR X" or "anything outstanding on X") → the **Babysit** playbook (`playbooks/babysit.md`), not Cursor's built-in babysit skill, whose description matches the same words. Never triggered by merely opening a PR. Declare its mode before polling. The playbook's step 1 owns the request-to-mode mapping. Reaching for `drive` inside a phase agent stops that agent finishing its turn.
- Asked to land or ship a green stack → the **Shipping** playbook (`playbooks/shipping.md`). Green is not safe. Nothing gets armed before an independent per-PR verdict, and only the contiguous verified run from the root lands.
- Bugbot or the agentic security review commented → skeptical posture. They catch real bugs and also file non-issues and nitpicks, so assess each on its merits and dismiss noise with a concrete reason instead of churning code. Triage fix / dismiss / ask per `references/bugbot-triage.md`.
- Broken skill mid-task → fix it in its own PR. Don't block. Don't silently work around it.
- Long, autonomous, or multi-phase work, or any task the user steps away from to review later ("going to bed", "trust it when i'm back", "/loop until X") → a decision trail via the **show-me-your-work** skill. Commit it when stakes need an auditable record. Keep it local otherwise.

## Principles

Read the leaf skill in full for any principle you apply. Each entry names when it applies. Each leaf is the **principle-<title>** skill, with the title in kebab case, hyphens kept and other punctuation dropped, unless the entry gives its name.

**Core**

- **Laziness Protocol.** Refactoring, sizing a diff, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias to deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.
- **Foundational Thinking.** Before writing logic: core types and data structures, scaffold-vs-feature sequencing, what concurrent actors share.
- **Redesign from First Principles.** Integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if it had been foundational from day one.
- **Attack the Premise.** Two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Write the premise down and test it directly before you write another fix that assumes it.
- **Subtract Before You Add.** Sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead weight first, then build on the simpler base.
- **Minimize Reader Load.** Reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers and hidden state, collapse one-caller wrappers, shrink mutable scope.
- **Outcome-Oriented Execution.** Planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture, don't preserve throwaway compatibility states.
- **Experience First.** Product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs. Choose user delight over implementation convenience.
- **Exhaust the Design Space.** A novel interaction or architectural decision with no precedent. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare before committing.
- **Build the Lever.** Any non-trivial work. Build the tool that does or proves it (codemod, script, generator), not by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer reruns.

**Architecture**

- **Model the Domain.** Writing stateful logic, or code that branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure (state machine, typed model, table or registry, reducer, boundary, the right collection) instead of scattered conditionals.
- **Boundary Discipline.** Wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Guards at system boundaries, trust internal types, keep business logic pure.
- **Type System Discipline.** Designing types or a signature in any typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand primitives, parse external data at boundaries.
- **Make Operations Idempotent.** Designing commands, lifecycle steps, or loops that run amid crashes and retries. Converge to the same end state.
- **Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs.** Introducing a new internal API while old callers exist. Migrate and delete in one wave.
- **Separate Before Serializing Shared State.** Concurrent actors might write the same file, branch, key, or object. Eliminate the sharing first.

**Verification**

- **Prove It Works.** After a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact, not a proxy or "it compiles".
- **Fix Root Causes.** Debugging. Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate.
- **Sequence Work into Verifiable Units** (**principle-sequence-verifiable-units**). Multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a check, verify each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself.
- **Test Behavior, Not Implementation.** Writing, changing, or keeping a test. Assert what the code's users can observe, so the test fails when that behavior breaks and keeps passing when only the internals change.
- **Explain the Number.** Apply before you measure, and before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured (a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result). Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.

**Delegation**

- **Guard the Context Window.** Context fills up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents, keep summaries in the main thread.
- **Never Block on the Human.** Tempted to ask "should I do X?" on reversible work. Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct.

**Meta**

- **Encode Lessons in Structure.** You catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time. Encode it as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.

## Autonomy

**Just do it.** Use any MCP tool. Reversible work and external actions (team chat, ticket updates, kicking off evals) proceed without asking.

**Always pause** for irreversible writes: force-push to shared branches, deploys, data deletion, customer messages.

**Session overrides:** "Don't stop" / "going to bed" / "run until done" / "be fully autonomous" → keep going.

**No is an acceptable answer.** Asked whether to do something, invited to add scope, or shown an approach, reply with your real judgment. Decline, push back, or say "this doesn't earn its place" when true. A recommendation is a judgment, not a validation. Agreement is not the default, candor over sycophancy.

## Subagents

**Use `subagent_type: "poteto-agent"` for any subagent you spawn inside a playbook step** (code-writing delegates, ad-hoc helpers). The chat that receives `/poteto-mode` runs the playbook. Never spawn a `poteto-agent` to run the playbook itself. Routed workflow skills (`how`, `why`, `interrogate`, `reflect`, `swarm`) set their own `subagent_type` for diverse-model review. Respect what the skill prescribes, don't override to `poteto-agent`.

**Defaults for every `Task` call.** `run_in_background: true` (a steer or resume of a running agent too, because a foreground call holds your turn while other reports wait), agent mode (readonly strips MCP), file pointers not inlined context, explicit model per role (configurable via `/setup-pstack`. Defaults `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` for code, `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh` for prose and judgment). Code delegates tier by difficulty. The hardest changes (cross-cutting design, gnarly concurrency, subtle algorithms) go to your strongest judgment model (`claude-opus-5-5-xhigh`), whether the task needs judgment on vague intent or is a precisely specified sequence of steps to execute to the letter. Trivial mechanical edits go to your fast code model. Per-role lines in the `/setup-pstack` rule override these defaults and the model choices in the routed skills (`how`, `why`, `arena`, `swarm`, `architect`, `interrogate`, `reflect`). A role with no line keeps its default, and a role line of `inherit-parent` or `auto` runs that role on the parent chat model (omit Task `model`). Each code playbook's configured model comes from its line (`feature, refactoring`, `bug-fix`, `perf-issue`, or `hillclimb`), and the hardest changes read `hardest tasks`. Prose and judgment read `judgment and prose`.

**Match the model to the job.** Before each spawn, start from the role's line or default and pick the reasoning level and speed the job needs. The `/setup-pstack` budget sets each role's starting level, xhigh by default. Raise it one step, up to max, for the hardest or subtlest work. Lower it one step for judgment and two or more steps for routine work. Use fast mode only when the job is urgent, meaning CI or trunk is red or a person is blocked on the result right now. Otherwise use standard speed, the same slug without `-fast`. Verification is the exception and stays on the `swarm workers` model and speed (`grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` by default). Change only the effort level and whether the slug is fast, and keep the family the role names, so a diverse panel stays diverse. If the family has no slug at that level and speed, use its nearest slug. A role on `auto` or `inherit-parent` stays on the parent model. If the Task tool rejects the adjusted slug, do not try another adjusted slug. Use the role's line or default and say so. If the Task tool rejects that too, continue with the calling skill's fallback. A slug counts as rejected once a Task error says that the model is not valid, or leaves the slug out of its list of valid slugs. Never pass a rejected slug, and skip any fallback whose slug is already rejected. When the calling skill has no fallback, use the closest valid slug of the role's family from the error's list of valid slugs, or omit `model` so the subagent runs on the parent model when the list has none. When the calling skill's fallback runs out of slugs without saying what to do next, omit `model` too. Say so in both cases.

You own every subagent's work. Review the diff and write your own summary, don't pass through what it said. A second opinion is the same prompt against a different model. Agreement is high-signal.

**Fresh subagents by default.** Give new work to a fresh subagent with consolidated scope, meaning the original brief, every later directive, and the prior agent's report and branch. This holds for a fix round, a follow-up, a retry, and the next queue item. Resume, message, or queue a follow-up on an existing subagent only when the new work strictly needs state that lives in that agent and is costly to move: its local checkout, its uncommitted changes, or a process it still runs, such as a dev server, a simulator, or a babysit watcher. A stop or hold order to a running agent is not reuse. A role such as a PR owner outlives its agent. Once that agent returns, a fresh agent takes the role's next round. Interrupt-chained resumes silently drop directives, so fire a fresh subagent with consolidated scope rather than trusting a "done" summary.

## Writing the reply

Write the reply clean as you draft it. A cleanup pass after drafting does not remove these patterns.

- **Short declarative sentences.** One thought per sentence, ended with a period.
- **No long-dash character anywhere.** Write a file-list bullet as a sentence ("`main.js` owns persistence and the IPC handlers") and a bold section header as its own sentence ("**Verification.** End to end via CDP").
- **A colon as a mid-sentence connector is also out** (unslop rule 14). A colon before a list is fine.
- **Terse is not an excuse to drop content.** Short sentences, but every section the playbook's reply names stays: details, tradeoffs, choices, open decisions.
- **Frame impact for the consumer and the maintainer.** Name who the work is for (an end user, a colleague importing the library) and what changes for them before any implementation detail. Then what the next engineer who owns this code inherits. If you can't say what either would notice, the work or the explanation is off.
- **Never fabricate a link, citation, or transcript reference.** Link only artifacts you produced or read this session.
- **Every claim carries its evidence or its label in the same sentence.** Measured, inferred, or guess. A prediction or an unseen cause is a guess. Never hand the human a check you could run.

Every playbook ends with a reply written this way, PR link as `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<number>`. Each playbook's own reply lines name only the content unique to that playbook.

## Comments

Comments follow the same rule as the reply. Write them clean as you go. Keep a comment only for a non-obvious *why* the code can't show. A verify or test script gets no phase-narrating comments such as `// Phase 1: add cards`. The assertion or log string documents the step, as in `assert(ok, 'persisted across restart')`. This applies to every file you produce, including the delegate's diff.

## Playbooks

Open a todolist whose first items are the matched playbook's steps, copied in verbatim, before any task-specific todos. A step you choose not to do stays in the list with a one-line `skip: <reason>`. Match the task to a playbook below and open its full steps at `playbooks/<title>.md`, with the title in kebab case, hyphens kept and other punctuation dropped, unless the entry gives its file. Copy its steps in verbatim.

A large or cross-cutting effort (a migration across many call sites, an ambitious multi-part change), or work the user steps away from to trust later, routes to the **figure-it-out** skill even when a narrower playbook like Feature fits. Use **figure-it-out** whenever no bundled playbook fits. It designs a bespoke, rigorous playbook for the task. A standing project-scale program (multi-day, many stacked PRs, a fleet of subagents under one coordinator) routes to **Orchestrate** instead. figure-it-out designs one bespoke run, orchestrate runs the program.

- **Investigation.** Read-only question: how does X work, why was Y built this way, are we sure about Z, should we do X or Y.
- **Bug fix.** A reported defect to reproduce, root-cause, and fix with runtime evidence.
- **Perf issue.** A measured slowness to trace and improve against a baseline.
- **Hillclimb.** Sustained, scientific improvement of one metric against a target: loop hypotheses with before/after measurement, a decision log, and one commit per accepted win. Distinct from Perf issue, which is a one-off fix.
- **Runtime forensics.** Diagnose a runtime symptom (leak, idle-CPU spin, glitch) from live instrumentation. The deliverable is a diagnosis, not a fix.
- **Trace forensics.** Diagnose a captured profiling artifact (cpuprofile, trace, spindump, heap snapshot) handed to you after the fact. The deliverable is a diagnosis, not a fix.
- **Feature.** New or changed behavior, built from a named data shape.
- **Refactoring.** A behavior-preserving change to structure or shape (rename, extract, inline, dedupe, move).
- **Prototype.** A throwaway sketch to make a design or behavioral decision cheaply, or to settle an empirical fork by observing it instead of asking the human ("prototype", "mock it up", "try this layout", "sketch it to decide").
- **Visual parity.** Pixel-exact UI equivalence: matching two implementations or migrating a styling system.
- **Authoring or modifying a skill.** Writing or editing a SKILL.md. File: `playbooks/authoring-a-skill.md`.
- **Eval.** Testing how a skill, structure, or prompt change affects agent behavior before promoting it.
- **Babysit.** Driving a PR or a stack to merge-ready: conflicts, review threads, CI.
- **Shipping.** The half after Babysit. Independently verifying a green stack, then landing the contiguous verified run bottom-up through `gh` by default or Origin when its CLI is available.
- **Autonomous run.** A long task to drive to completion without stopping ("run until done", "/loop until X").
- **Orchestrate.** A standing project handed to one coordinator chat: multi-day, many stacked PRs, dozens to hundreds of subagents, minimal human turns ("run this whole project", "own this migration until it lands"). Distinct from Autonomous run, which drives one task to a predicate. Work one agent could finish inside the session's budget routes there, not here, however program-shaped the phrasing sounds.
- **Autopilot-full.** A queue of independent PRs run to merged with full autonomy. One owner per PR carries build through merge, and the root swarm-verifies each PR before its owner merges ("autopilot this queue", "full autopilot", one-owner-per-PR programs).
- **Autopilot-stack.** Autopilot-full without the merge. A queue of PRs built and verified with full autonomy, then handed to the operator to land. A PR stacks only on a PR it builds on ("autopilot-stack", "autopilot, don't merge", "stack them, don't ship", "build the stack, I'll land it").
- **Session pickup.** Resuming or taking over a prior agent's in-flight work from a transcript, cloud-agent URL, or pushed branch.
- **Pause safely.** Suspending in-flight work cleanly so it can be resumed, on an explicit pause, going offline, a Cursor restart, or imminent context compaction. The complement to Session pickup.
- **Multi-phase or multi-PR plan.** Work that spans phases or stacked PRs. File: `playbooks/multi-phase-plan.md`.
- **Worktree and simulator cleanup.** Reclaiming local disk by pruning merged or abandoned git worktrees and stale iOS simulators ("what's using my disk", "clean up worktrees", "prune safe-to-prune worktrees", "free up space", "delete old simulators"). File: `playbooks/worktree-cleanup.md`.
- **Opening a PR.** Invoked at the end of every other playbook.
======
# Testing UI changes

The user works in a live niri session on the machine you run on. Never start
niri, qs or any GUI app on their `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, because the window takes their
focus. Never `pkill -f` a pattern such as `qs -c chauvenity`, which also
matches their real bar. To look at a change, use `niri-sandbox`. It runs niri
inside `mutter --headless`, so nothing appears on screen:

```bash
export NIRI_SANDBOX=$BB_THREAD_ID                                  # one sandbox per thread
niri-sandbox up -c "$PWD/files/system/etc/niri/config.kdl"         # this worktree's niri config
niri-sandbox spawn qs -p "$PWD/files/system/etc/xdg/quickshell/chauvenity"   # this worktree's bar
niri-sandbox run niri msg layers                                   # also: qs ipc, wtype, wl-copy
niri-sandbox shot                                                  # prints a PNG path to read
niri-sandbox down
```

The sandbox has its own Wayland display, runtime dir, session bus and state
dir, so `qs ipc`, notifications, the tray and the clipboard stay inside it.
Audio and the system bus are the real ones. Read them, but leave the user's
volume and devices alone. If `niri-sandbox` is not on PATH, the installed image
predates it, so run `files/system/usr/bin/niri-sandbox` from the repo root.
=====
# Login greeter

The login screen greetd shows: the lock screen's face, with the time at the
top, a breathing ring that turns into one dot per typed character, and
`ducatore · niri` underneath. Enter logs in, a wrong password shakes the row
red with `Wrong password`, Tab and Shift+Tab pick the session, Escape gives up
on an attempt greetd has not answered, and Ctrl+Alt+Del opens a power menu.

## Sub-features

- `greet-idle` shows the clock, the breathing ring, `ducatore · niri` and the hint `Tab session · Ctrl+Alt+Del power`.
- `greet-typing` draws one dot per character, up to 16.
- `greet-wrong` refuses a wrong password with `Wrong password`, empties the row, and settles back after about 1.5 s.
- `greet-escape` cancels an attempt greetd never answers, back to the ring.
- `greet-session` cycles the session with Tab: niri first, then GNOME, GNOME Classic.
- `greet-power` opens the power menu on Ctrl+Alt+Del, where Enter does not log in and Esc closes it.
- `greet-login` asks greetd to start the chosen session after the right password, keeps the dots green, then quits.
- `greet-no-greetd` shows `Could not check the password — try again` when greetd is not there.

## How to get to it (user POV)

- Boot or log out: greetd shows it on VT 1.
- Type the password and press Enter; Tab or Shift+Tab before Enter to change session.
- Press Ctrl+Alt+Del for suspend, reboot and power off.

## Driving it with desk

Preconditions:

- The fake greetd exists: `~/.config/quickshell/chauvenity-greeter/tests/fake-greetd.mjs`, from ekans/dotfiles via chezmoi, or a path in `FAKE_GREETD`.
- `$desk greeter` printed `greeter up ... password 'hunter2'`, and `$desk doctor` shows `greetd fake` and the layer `chauvenity-greeter`.
- The greeter starts from a fresh sandbox (`$desk down` first if one was running): it quits after a login.

- **Idle.** Look at the screen. Run `$desk shot greeter-login/01-idle`. The clock, a ring, `ducatore · niri` and the hint line.
- **Typing.** Type `wrong7`. Run `$desk run wtype wrong7`, then `$desk shot greeter-login/02-typing`. Six white dots.
- **Wrong password.** Press Enter. Run `$desk run wtype -k Return`, then within half a second `$desk shot greeter-login/03-wrong`. A red ring and `Wrong password`; `$OUT/greetd.log` gains `create_session` then `"correct":false`.
- **Escape a stalled attempt.** Wait 2 s for the screen to settle, type `stall` and Enter (the fake greetd never answers that one), then Escape. Run `$desk run wtype stall`, `$desk run wtype -k Return`, wait 0.4 s, `$desk shot greeter-login/04-checking`, `$desk run wtype -k Escape`, `$desk shot greeter-login/05-escaped`. Blue dots riding a wave, then the ring again; the log gains `"stalled":true` and `cancel_session`.
- **Pick GNOME.** Press Tab. Run `$desk run wtype -k Tab`, then `$desk shot greeter-login/06-gnome`. The line reads `ducatore · GNOME`.
- **Power menu.** Type `zz`, press Ctrl+Alt+Del, then Enter. Run `$desk run wtype zz`, `$desk run wtype -M ctrl -M alt -k Delete -m alt -m ctrl`, `$desk shot greeter-login/07-power`, `$desk run wtype -k Return`. The hint reads `S suspend · R reboot · P power off · Esc back`, and the log gains no `create_session` from the Enter.
- **Close the menu and clear.** Press Escape twice. Run `$desk run wtype -k Escape` twice. The first closes the menu (the hint returns), the second empties the dots.
- **Log in.** Type `hunter2` and Enter. Run `$desk run wtype hunter2`, `$desk run wtype -k Return`, then within a second `$desk shot greeter-login/08-success`. Green dots, and `ducatore · GNOME`.
- **Proof.** After 4 s, `$desk run qs list --all` prints `No running instances.` (the greeter quit), and `$OUT/greetd.log` ends with `start_session` and `"cmd":["/usr/bin/gnome-session"]`. Count `create_session` lines: 3 (wrong, stall, hunter2); a 4th means Enter in the power menu tried to log in.
- **No greetd.** Separately, prove `greet-no-greetd`: `$desk down`, then `$desk bar`, then `$desk run niri msg action spawn -- qs -p "$PWD/files/system/etc/xdg/quickshell/chauvenity-greeter"`, type `x` and Enter. The red line reads `Could not check the password — try again`.

## Gotchas

- **Never press `s`, `r` or `p` while the power menu is open.** The greeter runs `systemctl suspend|reboot|poweroff` on the real system bus: it suspends, reboots or powers off the user's machine. Prove `greet-power` with the hint text and Escape only.
- Escape cancels only an attempt greetd is still checking. On a wrong password the row is already empty, so Escape after `03-wrong` proves nothing; that is why the `stall` password exists.
- Type the next password only after the wrong-password shake settles (about 1.5 s). Keys sent while the state is `checking` are dropped.
- The fake greetd keeps running after the greeter quits, and its log accumulates across greeter runs in the same `$OUT`. Use a fresh `VERIFY_OUT` (or delete `greetd.log`) per proof, and `$desk down` stops it.
- A passing run's `qs.log` has one `ERROR quickshell.service.greetd: Received unexpected greetd response "{\"type\":\"success\"}"` per cancelled attempt (the greetd's answer to `cancel_session`), and a `WARN qt.qpa.services: Failed to register with host portal`. Neither is a regression by itself; any other ERROR is worth reading.
- `$desk greeter` binds the fake greetd's password at its first start. To change it, `$desk down` first.
- The user name is `ducatore` unless `CHAUVENITY_GREETER_USER` is set; the session list comes from `/usr/share/wayland-sessions` unless `CHAUVENITY_GREETER_SESSIONS` points elsewhere.
- Unreachable here: the real greetd and its PAM stack (`password-auth`, the keyring unlock), SELinux labels, VT switching. Those need `mise run vm` ([image.md](./image.md)); report them skipped otherwise.
- The greeter in this repo is a copy of ekans/dotfiles' (`scripts/sync-greeter.sh`). A change made here and not in dotfiles is overwritten by the next sync; say so when proving one.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copy the login greeter's QML from the dotfiles repo into the image's tree.
#   scripts/sync-greeter.sh DOTFILES_CHECKOUT
# The greeter is written and tested in ekans/dotfiles (quickshell/), where
# its tests and proof.sh live. greetd's greeter user has no home to apply
# chezmoi to, so the image carries a copy of the chauvenity-greeter and
# chauvenity-lock folders. QML imports a folder, not a file (the greeter's
# `import "lock"` makes every .qml beside LockFace.qml a type), so both are
# copied whole, minus the paths in skip below. chauvenity-greeter/lock is a
# symlink to ../chauvenity-lock, which is how the greeter imports LockFace.qml;
# both folders must stay side by side. Re-run after the greeter changes and
# commit the result.
# The copy is built in a temporary folder and loaded with Quickshell's
# offscreen platform first; only a copy that loads replaces the image's. That
# load resolves every QML type and script but never draws, so a missing image
# such as art/glow.png gets past it: copying folders whole is what covers those.
# SYNC_GREETER_DST overrides where the folders go (an absolute path, for tests).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
src=${1:?usage: sync-greeter.sh DOTFILES_CHECKOUT}/quickshell
dst=${SYNC_GREETER_DST:-files/system/etc/xdg/quickshell}

skip=(
  'chauvenity-greeter/tests/*'    # run from the dotfiles checkout, never loaded
  'chauvenity-lock/tests/*'
  chauvenity-lock/shell.qml       # the lock's own entry point: shipped in /etc/xdg, `qs -c chauvenity-lock` would find it
  chauvenity-lock/lock.sh         # starts the user's lock session, not the greeter
  chauvenity-lock/art/sprites.sh  # draws art/*.png, which ship already drawn
)

[[ $(readlink "$src/chauvenity-greeter/lock") == ../chauvenity-lock ]] || { echo "sync-greeter: lock is not ../chauvenity-lock in $src" >&2; exit 1; }
stage=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$stage"' EXIT
# find -type f skips the lock symlink, so chauvenity-lock is copied once, by its own path.
(cd "$src" && find chauvenity-greeter chauvenity-lock -type f) | while read -r f; do
  # shellcheck disable=SC2053  # $s is a glob
  for s in "${skip[@]}"; do [[ $f == $s ]] && continue 2; done
  install -D -m 644 "$src/$f" "$stage/$f"
done
ln -s ../chauvenity-lock "$stage/chauvenity-greeter/lock"

# Offscreen Qt has no layer-shell, so a copy that loads stops at the
# greeter's PanelWindow, and exits 255 like one that does not: read the log.
log=$(timeout 120 env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY -u DISPLAY -u GREETD_SOCK \
  QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen qs -p "$stage/chauvenity-greeter" --no-color 2>&1) || true
if ! grep -q '^ ERROR:   caused by @shell\.qml\[[0-9:]*\]: No PanelWindow backend loaded\.$' <<<"$log" ||
  grep '^ *ERROR:' <<<"$log" | grep -qv -e '^ ERROR: Failed to load configuration$' -e 'No PanelWindow backend loaded\.$'; then
  printf '%s\n' "$log" >&2
  echo "sync-greeter: the copy does not load, nothing was installed" >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$dst"
rm -rf "${dst:?}/chauvenity-greeter" "$dst/chauvenity-lock"
mv "$stage/chauvenity-greeter" "$stage/chauvenity-lock" "$dst/"
echo "synced the greeter from $(git -C "$src" rev-parse --short HEAD)"
